Marissa / Neha — reviewed the CSV and redaction doc. High-level recommendations: 

1) Model picks:
- Start lane: redwood/xl-compat-7B (good cost/latency tradeoff for most cases)
- Safety/priority routes: redwood/opt-improved-13B-quant (use for legal/contract prompts)
- Fallback: redwood-legacy-6B (cheap, but higher failure on nuance)

2) Eval plan (small pilot, ~2k prompts):
- Metrics: Exact-match where applicable, ROUGE-L for longer outputs, and a custom "redaction-safety" check to verify no PII leaks.
- Regression detection: baseline against the 7B on subset; alert on >5% drop in EM or any PII leakage.
- Run A/B over a 2-week window with traffic-sliced routes.

3) Prompt & redaction feedback:
- The CSV is mostly clean; recommend an extra column with "redaction_level" (none/mask/remove) so we don't guess.
- For multi-turn cases, add expected context-window trimming rules — some of their examples include full chat histories which would push tokens high.

Attachments: se_review_checklist.pdf (quick checklist for pilot).

I can spin up a lightweight eval harness (script + notebook) to run the pilot if you want — will need a HubSpot deal id and temporary API key for their test tenant.

Rafael
